 Live .  24,324 viewing 24324 viewing Live page Updated 6 minutes ago Five killed and a dozen more injured in Krakow shooting, police say 
 Police Say Five People Have Been Killed in Poland
 BBC News
 Close Watch live Summary
 Polish police say five people have been killed , and about a dozen more are injured, after a shooting in Krakow - what we know so far 
 Two police officers are among the injured , with one in a "critical condition", Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński says
 The area of the Main Market Square has been cordoned off and police are sending people away, says our reporter at the scene 
 Video shows gunshots ringing out in the square; images show emergency services at the scene 
 Police say the suspect - who was shot by officers - has been taken to hospital. Meanwhile, an interior ministry spokesperson says the suspect is a Polish citizen 
 In a social media post, Polish PM Donald Tusk calls the incident "tragic" and says he is being kept updated
 Close form Are you affected?
 Get in touch Media caption, Watch: Moment shooting heard in Krakow square Live Reporting
 Edited by Rorey Bosotti and Kieran Kelly, with Magda Mis reporting from Krakow
 Glass scattered across the floor after shop windows damaged in shooting published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 New images show police cordons in place along Krakow's Grodzka Street, which links Main Market Square to the Wawel Royal Castle on the Vistula River.
 Shop windows show signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.
 As our BBC Polska colleague Madga Mis reported earlier , there's still a heavy police presence in the area.
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image source, AFP via Getty Images

 'Do not exploit this tragedy,' says Tusk as he praises 'heroic' police published at 16:58 GMT 16:58 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Prime Minister Donald Tusk has praised the "heroic police officers who risked their lives" to stop today's shooter.
 As a reminder, the interior minister earlier confirmed two officers were shot - one remains "in very critical condition". 
 Tusk also appeals to colleagues "of all stripes: do not exploit this tragedy".
 "We will establish all the circumstances of this crime," he adds.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Suspect is Polish citizen - interior ministry official published at 16:50 GMT 16:50 GMT Breaking 
 Officials in Poland have identified the suspect as a Polish citizen, according to a press spokesperson for the country's interior ministry. 
 Malopolski Police adds that the only known perpetrator of the incident is in police custody, denying reports that another suspect is being sought.
 The police also deny reports that an officer has died.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 One police officer 'in very critical condition', says Polish interior minister published at 16:43 GMT 16:43 GMT Breaking 
 Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński says one of the police officers injured in today's shooting is "in very critical condition".
 Kierwiński says the officer suffered "three gunshot wounds" and "surgery is under way". He confirms a second officer was also shot.
 "Police officers in Krakow risked their lives to intervene. Immediately. Thanks to their heroic actions, the attacker was quickly apprehended," he writes on X.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Tram shot at before Main Market Square shooting - Krakow transport operator published at 16:38 GMT 16:38 GMT 
 A tram operating on route 1 of Krakow was shot at from "a passing car", the city of Krakow's official social media account says.
 Citing the Krakow's public transport operator MPK, the city's account says the shooting took place at All Saint's Square - a short walk from Main Market Square - and that the driver's cab window "was shattered".
 "None of the passengers or the driver were injured," the city adds.

 Watch: Moment gunshots ring out in Krakow's main square published at 16:31 GMT 16:31 GMT 
 Warning: This video contains distressing images 
 This footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment that gun shots were heard in Krakow's Main Market Square.

 Heavy police presence as Krakow's main square is unusually empty published at 16:29 GMT 16:29 GMT 
 Magda Mis 
BBC News Polska, in Krakow 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock There's a heavy police presence here in central Krakow, with the main square now cordoned off. I've also seen police officers driving around the city, as well as fire trucks and ambulances. 
 This is the main square in Krakow. It's very popular with tourists - there's a lot less of them around than in the summer but when I passed through several hours ago, the square was full of people. 
 It is surrounded by cafes, bars and restaurants and it's a Saturday so normally you would have a lot of people in there.
 Now, it's unusually empty as police are not letting anybody in. I can still see people coming out from behind the police cordon too, as officers are sending them away from the square.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I ran into a restaurant when the shooting started' published at 16:24 GMT 16:24 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters An eyewitness has described how she saw a man in a car who started shooting. 
 Tali tells Reuters news agency that she ran inside a restaurant and wanted to wait upstairs until they heard "silence". 
 But she says no silence came, because next she heard the noise of a helicopter - likely the emergency response. 
 "I don't know what to do now", she says, explaining that she doesn't know how best to get to her hotel. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Suspect was wearing 'military-style attire' - police spokesperson published at 16:16 GMT 16:16 GMT Breaking 
 We're hearing more from Polish police in Krakow.
 "According to information from police officers, the man was
wearing military-style attire," a police spokesperson says.
 "During the arrest, officers used their weapons, but
the man returned fire; as a result, two police officers are
among the injured." 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Bystanders gather as Main Market Square remains closed off published at 16:12 GMT 16:12 GMT 
 We're now getting more pictures from Krakow's Main Market Square, where the shooting unfolded.
 Pictures show members of the public observing the scene from behind a police cordon.
 Another photo shows a person waiting for treatment inside of a shop, the floor littered by glass shards.
 Image source, Reuters Image source, Reuters Image source, Reuters 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Market square cordoned off and police sending people away published at 16:01 GMT 16:01 GMT 
 Magda Mis 
BBC Polish, in Krakow 
 Image source, Getty Images The area of the Main Market Square has been cordoned off and police are sending people away from the streets leading to the square.
 There are a lot of police, but they say they won't talk to me.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'America stands with Poland at this dark hour' - US ambassador published at 15:56 GMT 15:56 GMT 
 We can now bring you comments from Tom Rose, the US ambassador to Poland, who says there has been a "horrific mass shooting in Krakow". 
 He describes it as a "savage and murderous attack that's shattered the peace of Poland". 
 "What we know so far is that several innocent precious lives were viciously cut down on a Saturday afternoon in Kraków’s historic and iconic central square," he says in a post on X. 
 "America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow. May the blessed memory of those lost today assuage the grief of those who mourn."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Polish President 'deeply concerned' published at 15:52 GMT 15:52 GMT Breaking 
 Polish President Karol Nawrocki says he is "deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events" in Krakow, and that his thoughts are with victims, those injured and their families.
 "I remain in contact with the relevant authorities and expect a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events," Nawrocki says in a post on X. 
 "The head of the National Security Bureau is on his way to Krakow. The safety of Poles is an absolute priority!" he adds.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Interior minister heading to the scene published at 15:50 GMT 15:50 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters Earlier, we heard that Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk was being kept informed by the Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński about the situation in Krakow. 
 We now hear that Kierwiński is heading to the scene in Krakow's Main Market Square, according to a spokesperson for the department. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What we do and don't know about the shooting in Krakow published at 15:44 GMT 15:44 GMT 
 Image source, Agencja Wyborcza.pl/Reuters What we know: 
 At least five people have been killed and about a dozen injured in a shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square, local police say
 The department says at around 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) a man drove into the square and began shooting "at random" from his car
 The perpetrator was shot by police and is being transported to hospital, the department adds
 Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is aware of the attack and is being kept informed by the country's interior ministry
 What we don't know: 
 Details of the number of victims and injuries are still being established, the official account for the city of Krakow says
 The identity and condition of the suspect
 A motive behind the attack
 The conditions of those who are injured
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Emergency personnel pictured in Krakow square published at 15:34 GMT 15:34 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters Image source, Getty Images Image source, Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/via REUTERS Image source, EPA/Shutterstock 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Tusk: Interior ministry providing updates published at 15:29 GMT 15:29 GMT 
 Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that he is "being kept informed by the Minister of the Interior about the situation in Kraków following the tragic shooting.
 "The police are investigating the background and all the circumstances of the attack."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Police say five people killed in shooting in Krakow published at 15:22 GMT 15:22 GMT Breaking 
 Five people have been killed after a shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square and around a dozen people are injured, including police officers, Małopolska Police say. 
 Posting on X, the police department says in a statement that at around 15:00 local time that a man who had driven onto the square began "firing at random people from his car".
 The perpetrator was shot by police and is being transported to hospital, another statement says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Emergency services responding and residents asked to avoid area published at 15:19 GMT 15:19 GMT 
 In a statement on social media, the official account for the city of Krakow writes:
 "Shots were fired in the Main Market Square. Emergency services are already on the scene. Police are also conducting an operation on Dietla Street. 
 "We are awaiting official confirmation of the scale of the incident, including information on the number of people injured." 
 The city is asking that residents avoid the area while police investigate.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Police responding to shooting in Krakow, Poland - reports published at 15:15 GMT 15:15 GMT Breaking 
 Police are responding to a shooting in Krakow, Poland, local authorities say.
 Polish media are reporting that two people have been killed and 10 others are injured, including police officers.
 This is a breaking news story - we'll bring you more information as it becomes available.
